item.title: Jingdezhen hails strategic guidance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Jingdezhen hails strategic guidance President's sustained attention steered porcelain capital's heritage list bid At a museum on the outskirts of Jingdezhen in Jiangxi province, children from nearby villages and visitors from across the country alike stand mesmerized as they witness the wonders of porcelain clay and ceramics in a spacious, brightly lit exhibition hall. Not too far away, unbroken stretches of lush forests thrive, hiding within them well-preserved ancient porcelain-stone mining sites. "The new museums and well-protected ancient sites are all the result of our efforts over the last few years while applying for World Heritage status," said Zhan Xinghua, deputy director of the Jingdezhen Municipal Culture, Radio, Television and Tourism Bureau. Zhan spent more than a decade working on the city's bid for a World Heritage listing. In July, the city, known as China's porcelain capital, succeeded in getting the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List. Zhan said the successful application for World Heritage listing could not have been achieved without President Xi Jinping's sustained attention to the city's ceramic culture. On Oct 11, 2023, Xi visited museums and ancient kiln sites in Jingdezhen. During the visit he emphasized on further growing and strengthening the ceramics sector to burnish the brilliant reputation of this "millennia-old porcelain capital" to an even greater luster. For Zhan, this was not an ordinary expectation. "It was Xi's sustained care and planning that allowed Jingdezhen to build up strength and succeed in making it to the World Heritage List, thereby filling the gap of a porcelain theme on the World Heritage list," he said. The decade-long bid process resulted in deep and comprehensive changes. Today, 196 ancient kiln sites are well protected, 108 historic alleys retain their original appearance, and 1,000-year-old porcelain-making skills continue to be passed down in an orderly manner. "From heritage protection to strategic empowerment, the president mapped out a clear growth path for Jingdezhen's World Heritage bid," said Zhan. In 2015, three experts wrote reports about the difficulties that lay in the path of protecting a large number of porcelain shards unearthed at the Imperial Kiln site in Jingdezhen. Within one year, Xi made two important instructions on protecting the site. He required that "we must protect, study and make good use of the Imperial Kiln ruins, this treasure of Chinese civilization". The principle of "rescue first" was then adopted. "While we were already protecting ancient kiln sites and historic neighborhoods, Xi's instructions formally launched a path of inheritance and protection aimed at World Heritage status," Zhan said. In July 2016, Xi commented on a proposal by cultural and museum experts on Liangzhu's World Heritage application. He said: "World Heritage applications should help highlight the historical and cultural value of Chinese civilization, embody the spiritual pursuits of the Chinese nation, and present to the world a full and authentic picture of ancient and modern China." These three principles became the overarching guide for China's cultural heritage applications and directly guided the entire process of Jingdezhen's bid. In a 2019 trip to Jiangxi, Xi proposed building a Jingdezhen National Ceramic Culture Inheritance and Innovation Pilot Zone and creating a new platform for international cultural exchanges. This upgraded Jingdezhen's bid from basic relic protection to a systematic project integrating heritage inheritance, industrial upgrading, talent gathering and international exchange. In Zhan's view, from the 2015 instruction on protecting the Imperial Kiln site to the 2023 field visit, the top-level guidance has been consistent and progressive, providing confidence for the city's World Heritage bid. Living inheritance of cultural heritage forms the core foundation of the successful bid, something Xi has also repeatedly stressed. In 2023, Xi visited the Taoyangli historical and cultural district in Jingdezhen and explored ancient kiln sites. While talking with inheritors of the intangible cultural heritage of porcelain making, he said that "the fine traditional culture passed down by our ancestors must remain firmly in our hands. We should keep pace with the times and carry it forward". Yu Yin, 36, comes from a porcelain-making family; his father and grandfather both worked in the trade. He watched Xi's inspection tour on television and was deeply impressed. Now, to attract more young people to the craft, he is trying to combine ceramics with popular culture. "In Jingdezhen, porcelain inheritance has never been the persistence of a few; it is the passion and pursuit of a whole group of people," he said. Unlike some other traditional intangible cultural heritage projects that face a decline in the number of practitioners and a lack of successors, Jingdezhen attracts young artists and craftspeople from across China and the world, who settle in the city and devote themselves to traditional skills and ceramic innovation. The city is now home to more than 3,400 inheritors of intangible cultural heritage, over 100,000 young creative entrepreneurs, and more than 6,000 "foreign Jingdezhen drifters" from other nations, who have come drawn by the city's reputation. Xie Dongxi, 35, who holds a PhD in ceramic design, came to the city as a university student and has since rooted herself there, researching and creating ceramic art. In her eyes, the World Heritage inscription is not an end point but a new starting point for Jingdezhen. "The World Heritage status has put a thousand-year-old ceramic culture on the world stage. It has not only raised the city's popularity but also built a golden bridge for ceramic cultural exchange and mutual learning between China and the world," Xie said. Xie is currently collaborating with an artist from Ghana on a co-creation that blends traditional Chinese ceramic aesthetics and porcelain-making techniques with overseas artistic concepts, allowing them to integrate and flourish together, thereby promoting ceramic culture beyond China and on the world stage. dengzhangyu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Holidays reveal huge appetite for overseas trips
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Holidays reveal huge appetite for overseas trips At the Piazzale Michelangelo in Florence, Italy, a street performer asked his audience where they came from. When he called out China, a sea of hands shot up amid cheers and applause. The scene was captured in one of the viral videos during this year's Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays that propelled the buzz phrase "the whole world knows China is on holiday" into a trending topic on Chinese social media. It also reflected a broader shift — Chinese tourists ventured further overseas, while international visitors continued to pour into China. China recorded 15.46 million inbound and outbound border crossings during the National Day holiday from Oct 1 to 7, up 6.7 percent year-on-year, according to the National Immigration Administration. Chinese mainland residents made 4.44 million outbound crossings, up 9.3 percent, while foreign nationals made 682,000 inbound entries, an increase of 5.4 percent. Of those foreign entries, 505,000 were visa-free, a rise of 9.2 percent. With the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday falling between Sept 25 and 27, travelers could take three days of annual leave to create a 13-day-long break, opening up opportunities for longer and more distant journeys. Europe was the leading long-haul destination for clients of the Beijing-based travel operator Utour Group during the National Day holiday, with a reported 140 percent year-on-year increase in Europe-bound travel bookings. The region accounted for nearly half of Utour Group's outbound business during the holiday period. Li Mengran, the company's marketing manager, said that demand for Europe, North America and Oceania reflected Chinese travelers' growing appetite for higher-quality overseas experiences. The growth, however, was uneven. Japan dropped out of the top 10 overseas destinations on travel platform Tuniu this year, after ranking first a year earlier. Indonesia, Turkiye and South Korea were among popular choices. Arrivals into Japan from the Chinese mainland fell 56.7 percent year-on-year to about 2.9 million in the first eight months, according to the Japan National Tourism Organization. Meanwhile, overseas visitors were increasingly discovering more of China. Trip.com Group reported double-digit growth in inbound travel during the combined holiday period, with bookings from Russia jumping 173 percent year-on-year. Britain, Malaysia and Canada each registered growth exceeding 50 percent. For some visitors, the festive atmosphere was itself an attraction. An Irish tourist identified as Alan told China Daily that activities planned across China during the National Day holiday had helped persuade him to visit. Wu Liyun, a professor at the China Academy of Culture and Tourism at Beijing International Studies University, attributed the growth to expanded visa-free policies, China's rising visibility on social media overseas and interest in experiencing Chinese festivities. lijing2009@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: 7.2-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
7.2-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama PANAMA CITY -- A 7.2-magnitude earthquake struck Panama on Friday, with its epicenter 39 kilometers northwest of Tonosi, a town in Los Santos province, according to a revised report from the University of Panama's Institute of Geosciences. Strong shaking was felt locally. Videos shared on social media showed the roof of the Albrook bus terminal swaying and windows shaking violently in several buildings. Tremors were felt in the capital, Panama City, a Xinhua correspondent in the city reported, with strong side-to-side jolts while sitting and a hanging light in a room swaying intensely. The United States Geological Survey, which initially reported a magnitude of 8.0, later revised its estimate to 7.7. The US Tsunami Warning System issued a tsunami threat following the earthquake, warning that hazardous tsunami waves were possible along parts of the coasts of Panama, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and Mexico within the next three hours. The U.S. tsunami warning was later revoked. The tsunami warning department of the Chilean Navy's Hydrographic and Oceanographic Service issued an alert, saying the earthquake could trigger a tsunami affecting the country's Easter Island. The Panama Canal Authority said operations were continuing normally after the earthquake struck. Emergency protocols had been activated, and technical teams were inspecting canal facilities for possible damage, it said in a statement. Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino urged the public to remain calm in a post on X. "What happened must not be used to spread alarm and disorder," he wrote. Mulino added that he had asked Government Minister Dinoska Montalvo for a report on the earthquake's impact. The Education Ministry suspended afternoon classes at all schools nationwide. Its administrative offices would also remain closed. No deaths or injuries have been reported so far among staff of Chinese companies and organizations or members of the local Chinese community following the earthquake.

item.title: US-Canada trade dispute rumbles on
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
US-Canada trade dispute rumbles on Alcohol, dairy, motorcycle firms face fresh uncertainty as new ban kicks in A US ban on nearly $1 billion worth of Canadian imports has done little to ease a trade dispute between the two countries, analysts said, with talks showing limited progress and US President Donald Trump saying he is in no rush to resume negotiations. The ban, which took effect Sept 29, includes alcoholic beverages, dairy products and motorcycles, and is adding pressure on Canadian businesses that rely heavily on the US market, particularly smaller producers already facing high tariffs. Trump said on Monday that he was "in no rush" to restart trade talks with Canada. On Wednesday, he said Ottawa had been "very difficult to deal with" and that Washington was not satisfied with the terms currently on the table. The measure is relatively small compared to the roughly $880 billion in annual two-way trade between the two countries. "The direct impact on the overall Canada-US trade relationship is fairly small because the products covered by the ban represent only a small share of total bilateral trade," said Mesbah Fathy Sharaf, an economics professor at the University of Alberta. "However, the impact could be much more serious for the Canadian companies directly affected, especially smaller producers that depend heavily on the US market," Sharaf told China Daily. "The wider concern is that the ban adds another layer of uncertainty to an already tense trade relationship," he said. Ronald Stagg, a history professor at Toronto Metropolitan University, similarly said the nearly $1 billion figure should be viewed in the context of the much larger bilateral trading relationship. "One billion is not much in the total amount of trade, but if you are a small businessperson who does a sizable amount of business with the US, this can be a serious issue," Stagg told China Daily. "Federal supports for industries hurt by tariffs generally do not cover smaller players," he said, adding that previous tariffs had already prompted some small companies to consider opening branch plants in the United States, "a costly and time-consuming measure". The US restrictions came after months of escalating tariffs and retaliatory measures between the two countries. Sharaf said the additional damage from the ban "may be limited because many of these products were already facing very high tariffs". "In some cases, the tariffs had already made it difficult for Canadian producers to compete in the US market," he said. But he said an import ban was fundamentally different from a tariff. "With a tariff, companies can continue selling if buyers are willing to pay the higher price. A ban closes the market completely," Sharaf said. "For some producers, especially those with few alternative export markets, that difference could be important." The costs of the restrictions could also extend beyond Canadian exporters, he said. "Canadian producers are likely to feel the immediate impact because they lose access to an important market," Sharaf said. "US importers and distributors that rely on these products will also face costs." "American consumers may see fewer choices and, in some cases, higher prices if the products are difficult to replace," he said. "So the cost will be shared, although it will not be shared equally." From tariffs to restrictions The ban also represents a further shift from tariffs to outright restrictions on trade. "I am not sure why the shift from tariffs to the outright banning of certain imports has taken place," Stagg said. "It may simply represent added pressure on Canada." Sharaf said Washington had significant leverage because of the importance of the US market to Canadian exporters. "The United States has significant bargaining power because the US market is extremely important for Canadian exporters. That gives Washington leverage in negotiations," he said. But the two economies remain closely intertwined, he said. "Canadian and American businesses depend on each other through trade and cross-border supply chains. For that reason, prolonged trade restrictions can create costs on both sides," Sharaf said. Trump's shifting comments on the timing of a deal have drawn skepticism from both experts. Sharaf said he viewed Trump's three- or four-week timetable primarily as a negotiating tactic rather than evidence that an agreement was imminent. "From an economic perspective, trade disputes rarely end with one side simply winning everything. They usually involve concessions and costs for both sides," he said. Stagg was even more skeptical of Trump's comments. "Trump's comments are typical of how he deals with a situation that is not going his way, say, for example, the confrontation with Iran," Stagg said. "The comments don't really mean anything. They are just to keep his critics silenced." He said Trump's remarks should not be interpreted as evidence that negotiations were advancing. "Only an acknowledgment by the Canadian government that the two sides are near to a deal would indicate progress," he said.

item.title: China names largest overseas Asian Para Games squad
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
China names largest overseas Asian Para Games delegation China has named a 500-member delegation, including 312 athletes, for the fifth Asian Para Games, which will be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Oct 18 to 24. The delegation was established in Beijing on Saturday by the China Disabled Persons' Federation. China will compete in 17 sports and 335 events, marking the country's largest athlete delegation to an Asian Para Games held outside China. The 312 athletes comprise 146 men and 166 women from 25 provincial-level regions and 13 ethnic groups. They have an average age of 28.8, with the oldest aged 50 and the youngest 16, according to the organizers. All the athletes are amateurs and come from diverse backgrounds, including factory workers, students, office employees and freelancers. The Games will feature 18 sports and 502 events, including athletics, swimming, table tennis, wheelchair fencing, blind football, wheelchair basketball and sitting volleyball. More than 3,000 athletes from 45 countries and regions are expected to compete.

item.title: Tibetan postman delivers Long March spirit across grasslands
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Tibetan postman delivers Long March spirit across grasslands Share - WeChat
On wind-scoured grasslands where Red Army troops trekked 90 years ago during the Long March, ethnic Tibetan postman Lhalung Dorje brings postal service to remote herding communities in Sichuan province. He covers the 3,500-meter-high "Long March mail route" in Zoige county, braving blizzards and boggy marshland through all seasons. Over 19 years on the job, he has logged nearly 580,000 kilometers and delivered more than 5 million pieces of mail without a single mistake, embodying the Long March spirit as a tireless messenger across the grasslands.

Xi on carrying forward Long March spirit Share - WeChat
This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, which lasted from 1934 to 1936. The arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. President Xi Jinping has always stressed the importance of carrying forward the spirit of the Long March, which has become a powerful spiritual force inspiring the Chinese people to overcome difficulties and advance from victory to victory.

item.title: Gen Z finds a sweet future in hometown's green transition
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Gen Z returnee finds a sweet future in hometown's green transition At the southern foot of the Jinggang Mountains in Ji'an, Jiangxi province, the buzz of bees is becoming part of a new soundscape. Tianhe town once relied on coal mining as the backbone of the local economy. Today, as the town looks for greener ways forward, a young beekeeper is betting on an old family trade — with some new ideas of his own. Mao Yuanxiang, a Gen Z returnee, could have started his career in Shenzhen after graduating from university with a degree in cost engineering. Instead, he returned home. He chose beekeeping, an industry his family has been involved in for generations, and set about giving it a modern twist. Working with universities, Mao has introduced smart beehives and explored the development of honey-based drinks. He is also planning a bee-themed park where visitors can learn about beekeeping and the natural environment behind it. His story is part of a broader transformation taking place across Jinggangshan. Known as the cradle of the Chinese revolution, Jinggangshan is where Chinese revolutionaries explored a new path. The experience gave rise to the Jinggangshan Spirit, commonly described as a spirit of firm faith and hard work, seeking truth from facts and forging new paths, relying on the people and striving for victory. Tune in to the second episode of China Daily's documentary series Aspiration: One in a Hundred Million and follow reporter Yan An as she visits Tianhe town to meet Mao, a young Party member who is forging a new path back home. Related: What are CPC members really like? A visit to the Party's birthplace reveals the answer

item.title: Flame lit in Turin for Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Flame lit in Turin for Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade The flame for the 33rd Winter World University Games to be held in Changchun, northeastern China's Jilin province, was lit in Turin, Italy, on Thursday, marking another milestone in preparations for the event to be held early next year. At a ceremony held at the University of Turin, a torch from 1959, the year the first-ever Universiade was hosted by the city, was used to light the cauldron, from which the Changchun 2027 flame lantern was ignited. Gu Gang, mayor of Changchun, vice-chairman of the Organizing Committee for the 2027 Winter World University Games and chairman of its Executive Committee, handed the lantern to a flame bearer. The lantern was then carried through the streets of Turin. "Though thousands of miles apart, Changchun and Turin are now connected by the flame collection ceremony, united in youth and bound by sports," Gu said in an address. "With the flame as our bond and ice and snow as our medium, let's build a bridge of cultural exchange between East and West, bringing young people from all over the world closer together in mutual understanding and shared progress." "FISU stands for education, culture and sport, and Changchun is making every effort to provide an excellent mixture of these three elements," Leonz Eder, president of the International University Sports Federation, said. "The event will be a world-class sporting competition supported by excellent facilities, a high-quality international academic conference and cultural exchange programs that will allow students from around the world to experience the beauty of the province and the city, particularly its winter festival," he added. "Sports is a powerful way to bring people together," said Cristina Prandi, rector of the University of Turin, which has been home to the Universiade's permanent ceremonial cauldron, the "Flame of Knowledge", since 2018. "This is particularly important for us because participating in sports activities helps our international students connect with one another, and feel a part of the university community." Emanuele Ughetto, a local student who has studied Chinese for a long time and volunteered as a translator for the flame collection event, said that he was very happy to be picked for the ceremony. "I'm so excited to participate in such a grand event of transferring the flame to my motherland," said Yang Beishu, a Chinese conductor who lives in Turin. "The spirit of sports is a bond that links European people with Chinese people, as well as us overseas Chinese with our home," she said. The flame-lighting ceremony came a day after Changchun marked the 100-day countdown to the opening of the Games on Jan 15. With just over three months to go, Gao Jifeng, director of the Changchun Municipal Sports Bureau and deputy director of the Office of the Changchun 2027 Executive Committee, said preparations have entered the operational phase. Rather than building new competition venues, organizers have focused on upgrading existing facilities across the Changchun and Jilin competition zones, Gao said, adding that venue upgrades are now nearing completion, competition equipment is ready and schedules and lists of volunteers have been finalized. The flame will leave Turin and arrive in Changchun in mid-October. "In 99 days, student-athletes from around the world will gather in Changchun to challenge themselves and push their limits on ice and snow. May young people compete with courage and deepen their bonds through sport. May passion for sport cross all borders, dreams illuminate one another, and friendship endure for generations to come," said Gu. "We have seen the vibrant energy of Changchun, the warmth and hospitality of its people, and the truly remarkable progress achieved in such a short space of time. Let's meet in Changchun at its finest," said Eder, the president of FISU.
